ιαειροσ.def: Jairus, a Jewish ruler of the synagogue.

ιακωβ.def: (Hebrew), Jacob, (a) the patriarch, son of Isaac, (b) father of Joseph, the husband of Mary.

ιακωβοσ.def: James, (a) the Small, son of Alphaeus, and one of the Twelve, (b) half-brother of Jesus, (c) father (?) of Jude, (d) son of Zebedee, and brother of John, one of the Twelve, killed A.D. 44.

ιαμβρησ.def: Jambres, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh.

ιαννα.def: Jannai, an ancestor of Jesus; Jannai was the son of Joseph, and father of Melchi.

ιαννησ.def: Jannes, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh.

ιαομαι.def: I heal, generally of the physical, sometimes of spiritual, disease.

ιαρεδ.def: (Hebrew), Jared, son of Mahalalel and father of Enoch.

ιασων.def: Jason, a Christian of Thessalonica, perhaps the same as the "relative" of Paul.

ιδιοσ.def: one's own, belonging to one, private, personal; one's own people, one's own family, home, property.

ιδιωτησ.def: (unofficial, hence) an amateur, an unprofessional man, a layman; an ungifted person.

ιδουμαια.def: Idumea, Edom, a district of Arabia, immediately south of Judea.

ιεζαβελ.def: Jezebel, name given to a false prophetess of Thyatira, possibly borrowed from the name of Ahab's wife, queen of Israel.

ιεραπολισ.def: Hierapolis, a city of the Lycus valley in Phrygia, near Laodicea and Colossae.

ιερατεια.def: the duty (office) of a priest, priesthood.

ιερατευμα.gloss: the act or office of priesthood
ιερατευμα.def: the act or office of priesthood.

ιερευσ.def: a priest, one who offers sacrifice to a god (in Jewish and pagan religions; of Christians only met.).

ιεριχω.def: Jericho, a city a little north of the Dead Sea.

ιερον.def: a temple, either the whole building, or specifically the outer courts, open to worshippers.

ιεροπρεπησ.gloss: suitable to a sacred character, reverent
ιεροπρεπησ.def: suitable to a sacred character, reverent.

ιεροσολυμα.def: the Greek form of the Hebrew name: Jerusalem.

ιεροσυλεω.def: I commit sacrilege, rob a temple.

ιεροσυλοσ.def: robbing temples, but possibly simply: sacrilegious.

ιερουσαλημ.def: (Aramaic form), Jerusalem, the capital of Palestine: hence Judaism, and allegorically, Christendom, the Christian Church.

ιερωσυνη.def: the abstract notion of the priestly office.

ιεσσαι.def: (Hebrew), Jesse, son of Obed, and father of King David.

ιεφθαε.def: (Hebrew), Jephthah, one of the Judges of Israel.

ιεχονιασ.def: (Hebrew), Jechoniah, son of Josiah and father of Salathiel.

ιησουσ.def: Jesus; the Greek form of Joshua; Jesus, son of Eliezer; Jesus, surnamed Justus.

ικανοσ.def: (a) considerable, sufficient, of number, quantity, time, (b) of persons: sufficiently strong (good, etc.), worthy, suitable, with various constructions, (c) many, much.

ικανοω.def: I make sufficient, render fit, qualify.

ικετηρια.def: (originally: the olive branch held in the hand of the suppliant), supplication, entreaty.

ικονιον.def: Iconium, a Phrygian city of the Roman province Galatia (modern Konia).

ιλασκομαι.def: (a) I have mercy on, show favor to, (b) trans. with object of sins: I forgive, pardon.

ιλασμοσ.def: a propitiation (of an angry god), atoning sacrifice.

ιλαστηριον.def: (a) a sin offering, by which the wrath of the deity shall be appeased; a means of propitiation, (b) the covering of the ark, which was sprinkled with the atoning blood on the Day of Atonement.

ιλλυρικον.def: Illyricum, a Roman province, afterwards called Dalmatia, bounded by Pannonia on the north, Macedonia on the south, Moesia on the east, and the Adriatic Sea on the west.

ιμασ.def: a thong, strap, (a) for binding a man who is to be flogged, (b) for fastening a sandal or shoe.

ιματιζω.def: I clothe, provide clothing for; pass: I am clothed.

ιματιον.def: a long flowing outer garment, tunic.

ιοππη.def: Joppa, a coast town of Judea, west-north-west of Jerusalem.

ιορδανησ.def: the Jordan, a great river flowing due south and bounding Galilee, Samaria, and Judea on the east.

ιουδαια.def: Judea, a Roman province, capital Jerusalem.

ιουδαιζω.def: I live as a Jew (in religion, ceremonially).

ιουδαικωσ.def: in the manner of Jews (religiously, ceremonially).

ιουλια.def: Julia, a Roman Christian, probably a slave or freed from the Imperial household.

ιουλιοσ.def: Julius, a Roman centurion on special service.

ιουστοσ.def: Justus, (a) a surname of Joseph Barsabbas, one of the two nominated to fill Judas' place as apostle, (b) Titius Justus, a Corinthian Christian, (c) surname of Jesus, a Christian with Paul in Rome.

ιππευσ.def: a horse-soldier, a mounted soldier, a cavalryman.

ισαγγελοσ.def: equal to or like the angels.

ισοψυχοσ.def: like-minded, of the same mind or spirit.

ισραηλ.def: (Hebrew), Israel, surname of Jacob, then the Jewish people, the people of God.

ισραηλιτησ.def: an Israelite, one of the chosen people of Israel, a Jew.

ιστημι.def: trans: (a) I make to stand, place, set up, establish, appoint; mid: I place myself, stand, (b) I set in balance, weigh; intrans: (c) I stand, stand by, stand still; met: I stand ready, stand firm, am steadfast.

ισχυροσ.def: strong (originally and generally of physical strength); mighty, powerful, vehement, sure.

ισχυω.def: I have strength, am strong, am in full health and vigor, am able; meton: I prevail.

ισωσ.def: perhaps, equally; it may be that.

ιτουραιοσ.def: Ituraean, an adjective applied to a district also called Trachonitis, about 60 miles east of the Sea of Galilee, and partly inhabited by the nomad tribe called Ituraeans.

ιωαθαμ.def: Jotham, son of Uzziah and father of Ahaz.

ιωαννα.def: (Hebrew), Joanna, Johanna, wife of Chuza, Herod's steward.

ιωαννησ.def: John: the Baptist, the apostle, a member of the Sanhedrin, or John Mark.

ιωβ.def: (Hebrew), Job, the hero of the book of that name in the Old Testament.

ιωραμ.def: (Hebrew), Joram, Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat and father of Uzziah.

ιωσαφατ.def: (Hebrew), Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, son of Asaph, father of Joram, an ancestor of Jesus.

ιωση.def: (Hebrew), gen. case of Joses (a) son of Eliezer, (b) son of Mary, brother of Jesus, (c) surnamed Barnabas (also called Joseph).

ιωσησ.def: (Hebrew), Joses (a) son of Eliezer, (b) son of Mary, half-brother of Jesus, (c) surnamed Barnabas (also called Joseph).

ιωτα.gloss: a small letter of the Greek alphabet
ιωτα.def: iota, a small letter of the Greek alphabet, used in the NT (like yod, the Hebrew or rather Aramaic letter which was the smallest of all) to indicate the smallest part.
